name: Eplerenone
summary: A selective aldosterone receptor antagonist with proven mortality benefit in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EMPHASIS-HF) and post-MI left ventricular dysfunction (EPHESUS), with fewer hormonal side effects than spironolactone.
mechanism: Selectively blocks the mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptor in the distal nephron, increasing sodium and water excretion while retaining potassium; also attenuates aldosterone-driven cardiac fibrosis.

dosing.adult: Heart failure: 25 mg once daily, increased to 50 mg once daily if potassium allows; hypertension: 50 mg once daily

safety.pregnancy: Category B (no teratogenicity in animal studies)
warnings: Hyperkalemia is the key risk — highest with ACE inhibitors/ARBs, potassium supplements, and NSAIDs
Avoid as add-on to ACE inhibitor plus ARB in type 2 diabetes with microalbuminuria
monitoring: Serum potassium and creatinine at baseline, 1 week, 1 month, then periodically
safety.overdose: Hyperkalemia; treat with insulin/glucose, potassium binders, and dialysis if severe.

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (NYHA II–IV)
Left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction
clinicalPearls: Selectivity for the mineralocorticoid receptor means far less gynecomastia and mastalgia than spironolactone.
The classic mistake is starting it with K+ >5.0 mEq/L — check potassium before and during therapy.
good: HFrEF and resistant hypertension when hormonal side effects of spironolactone are a problem.
bad: Hyperkalemia, CrCl <30 mL/min, or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references (Goodman & Gilman, Katzung, Lexicomp-level standard facts). Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
